title: Dangling on purpose
description:
Write three small bugs with pointers, explain each, then fix them.

```
bug 1: returning the address of a local -> fixed by returning a value
bug 2: using a pointer after delete      -> fixed by setting it to nullptr and checking
bug 3: pointer into a vector that grew   -> fixed by keeping an index
```
hints: After `delete p;`, `p` still holds the old address; reading `*p` is undefined behaviour (lesson 1.05).
`-fsanitize=address` reports "stack-use-after-return" or "heap-use-after-free" with the exact line.
requirements: Each bug is in its own function, commented out or behind a `bool runBugs{false};`, so the program stays safe.
Each fixed version runs and prints its result.
If your build has the address sanitizer, run the bugs once with it and copy one line of its report into a comment.
stretch: Add bug 4: a pointer to a `std::string`'s characters after the string changes.
